title: Token Unlocks: Why a Token's Supply Can Grow on a Schedule
summary: Many tokens do not put their whole supply into circulation at launch. Allocations for the team, early backers, the treasury and ecosystem funds are often locked and released over months or years under a vesting schedule set out in the project's documents or smart contracts.
blocks: Many tokens do not put their whole supply into circulation at launch. Allocations for the team, early backers, the treasury and ecosystem funds are often locked and released over months or years under a vesting schedule set out in the project's documents or smart contracts.

An unlock is the moment a tranche of that locked supply becomes transferable. Some schedules release a large block at once after an initial waiting period, known as a cliff; others release smaller amounts continuously, usually called linear vesting.

This is why circulating supply and fully diluted supply can differ so much. Market capitalisation reflects only the tokens circulating today, while the fully diluted figure counts every token that will eventually exist, including those still locked.

Unlock calendars are generally public, and trackers compile them from project disclosures. An unlock does not by itself determine what a price does — recipients may hold, stake or move their tokens — but the schedule explains why the number of tokens in circulation changes over time.
